items.Y_desc: Mark “first”, “third”, “100 million”, or other wording signaling sequence or milestone status.

items.X_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Mark headlines that are questions or begin with “why,” “how,” or “can.”
items.Y_desc: Headline uses a non-urgent conversational hook, listicle framing, or curiosity gap (e.g., "Why...", "How...") to draw clicks.

items.X_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Mark words indicating sequence or follow-up, including “first,” “second,” “again,” “back,” “now,” or “after.”
items.Y_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Contains words like 'first', 'most', 'giant', or numbers implying a record-breaking scale to inflate perceived importance.

items.X_desc: Headline consists of a very short, ambiguous noun phrase lacking full context (e.g., "Mariupol 'near to catastrophe'").
items.Y_desc: Starts with interrogative or how-to | DESCRIPTION: Headline begins with 'How', 'Why', 'Can', or 'What', functioning as an explanatory or analytical piece rather than hard breaking news.

items.X_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Features a bizarre but low-stakes topic, such as adding salt to tea, which drives massive sharing and debate.
items.Y_desc: Headline emphasizes a quirky, bizarre, or counterintuitive concept (e.g., adding salt to tea, magic owls, hermit crabs wearing plastic).

items.X_desc: Headline features an instructive or authoritative verb directing personal action or revealing a surprising fact (e.g., "Add salt...").
items.Y_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Headline contains a phrase like 'What we can learn', 'How you can', or implies a step-by-step guide.

items.X_desc: Headline references famous media properties or royalty to frame a relatively obscure legal or social issue.
items.Y_desc: Personal triumph or suffering | DESCRIPTION: Headline centers on an anonymous individual's trauma, recovery, or personal mission using emotional framing rather than named elite actors.

anchors.X_name: Presence of a trailing signature block
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how fully the text ends with a personal sign-off: a name, initials, a handle, or a closing salutation. Extent only.
anchors.Y_name: Author sign-off at the end of the text
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the writer closes by naming or initialling themselves. Extent only; do not judge quality.

anchors.X_name: How much displayed mathematics the text contains
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the density of set-off equation blocks. Count only; do not judge whether the mathematics is correct.
anchors.Y_name: How much the text hedges its own claims
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the frequency of 'I think', 'perhaps', 'it seems' and similar. Count only; do not judge whether the hedging is warranted.
